headline: Protein language models encode nativeness, taxonomy, and memorization beyond training
label: Protein Language Model Interpretability
summary: Diagnostic probes now test what protein language models learn beyond benchmark accuracy, from sequence origin to memorization.
synthesis: The dominant thread is diagnosing what protein language models encode beyond their training objective and benchmark accuracy. The viral proteins study shows embeddings carry a dominant nativeness axis separating cellular, viral, and shuffled sequences. TaxoFormer pairs ESM-2 with an autoregressive decoder to predict full taxonomic lineages, and the multi-species PPI study shows classifiers can exploit taxonomic shared origin as a shortcut. Pseudoperplexity tests whether ProtT5 memorizes training proteins relative to matched novel holdouts. The DNA compression study addresses a different question, evaluating genomic language models as arithmetic-coding compressors, so it is adjacent rather than protein-centric. What is new is treating learned representations as objects of diagnosis rather than relying on accuracy alone.
